options.explanation: Correct. A non-obstante clause is an overriding provision; where two such clauses compete, the court harmonises first and then prefers the more special provision.

questions.stem: Priya argues that the proviso to section 12 shows that the section as a whole is concerned only with structural work, so painting the facade cannot be caught. The correct analysis is:
questions.sourceRef: Internal aids — proviso and Explanation

options.text: She is right: a proviso indicates the true scope of the section it qualifies
options.explanation: A proviso does not fix the scope of the section; it carves an exception out of what would otherwise have been within it.

options.text: She is right, because an Explanation cannot create liability where the main provision does not
options.explanation: An Explanation clarifies and may widen or narrow the main provision; here it makes explicit that painting over an original facade is disfigurement, which the Act's preamble shows was always within its object.

options.text: She is wrong: a proviso carves an exception out of the main provision and cannot be used to enlarge or redefine it, while the Explanation expressly deems painting over the facade to be disfigurement, so her act is caught and only the certified parapet removal is protected
options.explanation: Correct. Three internal-aid points combine — a proviso is limited to the provision it is attached to and is not an independent enactment; an Explanation is read with, not apart from, its section; and the preamble confirms that disfigurement is within the object of the Act.

options.text: She is wrong, because a proviso is always to be read as an independent enactment of general application
options.explanation: This states the opposite of the rule. A proviso is never to be read as an independent enactment.

questions.stem: Priya also relies on the marginal note 'Restriction on demolition' to argue that section 12 cannot touch painting. This argument:
questions.sourceRef: Internal aids — marginal notes and preamble

options.text: Succeeds, because a marginal note is part of the Act and controls the section beside it
options.explanation: A marginal note is the weakest internal aid and is generally no part of the Act, not having been inserted by the legislature.

options.text: Fails: a marginal note is the weakest internal aid, generally no part of the Act, and cannot control the plain words of the section, which the Explanation makes plainer still
options.explanation: Correct. Marginal notes are used at most as a rough indication; here the section's own Explanation settles the point, and the preamble confirms that disfigurement is within the Act's object.

options.text: Succeeds, because internal aids rank above external aids and must be given effect
options.explanation: Ranking internal above external aids says nothing about whether a marginal note can override a section. It cannot.

options.text: Fails, but only because the Second Schedule contradicts the marginal note
options.explanation: The Second Schedule prescribes the form of a notice under section 19 and is irrelevant to section 12.

questions.stem: The building removed from the list after seven days' notice: what is the effect of the shortfall under section 19?
questions.sourceRef: Mandatory and directory provisions — negative language, individual safeguard, prejudice

options.text: The removal is invalid: section 19 is mandatory — it is expressed in negative and prohibitory form, it confers a safeguard on an identified individual, and the shortfall causes obvious prejudice to the owner
options.explanation: Correct. All three indicators point the same way, and where a provision is mandatory, non-compliance invalidates the act done.

options.text: The removal is valid, because section 19 uses 'shall' and 'shall' is directory unless the statute says the act is void
options.explanation: Neither limb is right: 'shall' is not conclusive either way, and the absence of an express avoidance clause does not make a provision directory.

options.text: The removal is valid, because the owner suffered no financial loss
options.explanation: Prejudice is not confined to financial loss; the loss of the statutory hearing is itself the prejudice.

options.text: The removal is valid, because the notice was in the form prescribed by the Second Schedule
options.explanation: Using the prescribed form does not cure a shortfall in the period of notice, which is the requirement section 19 actually imposes.
